results.quote: For every \(17\le k\le n\), it follows: \(lcc(g_k^n)>1\).
For every \(i\ge 1\) and n=2^i there exists a protocol that solves (n,n)-counting with a local communication complexity of 11.
This protocol can be used to compute any symmetric boolean function with the same local complexity.
For every n and k, such that \(0\le k\le n/10\), there exists a protocol that solves (n,k)-counting with a local communication complexity of 2.
The sorting of 1-bit inputs can be solved with local complexity 12.
For every network size n=2^i and search location k≤n, searching for the kth 1 can be solved with constant local complexity.

results.problem: modular arithmetic operations (comparison, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation mod n+1)
results.quote: Suppose n+1 is a prime number. A balanced 2-symmetric function f:{0,1}^{2n}→N can be computed with constant local complexity if the corresponding function g_f:[n]×[n]→N is: 1. a function of only one of the two variables with range {0,1,...,n}, 2. comparison operator (>,≥,=,≤,<) on two variables with output 0 or 1, 3. a modular (mod (n+1)) addition, subtraction, multiplication or division, exponentiation or 4. a constant applications/composition of functions from first three items in this list.
For \(1\le x,y\le n\), the local complexity of computing GCD(x,y) is O(1).
